# Unified Delivery Ingress and Consumer-Time Presentation

<!-- spec-coder:artifact-v1 spec -->

Status: Gate 1 design, Gate 2 specification, and Gate 3 implementation plan approved.

## Problem Statement

The outbound architecture is durable-first, but its unification boundary is too
late. Producers currently render and prepare Gateway work before the per-scope
Delivery Ring receives it. The Ring therefore standardizes scheduling and
execution only after Turn Card, Worker, Answer, recovery, and notification
paths have already selected different identity, rendering, checkpoint, and
settlement protocols.

The resulting problems are observable rather than cosmetic:

- a successful Turn Card Gateway acknowledgement settles the Outbox Entry
  before a process-local checkpoint callback settles the Conversation Page, so
  a crash may require ordinary success to pass through recovery;
- Turn Card execution is selected by formatted `projection_key` conventions
  instead of a typed Delivery Subject;
- current rendering determines durable pagination boundaries, so presentation
  changes can affect restart recovery;
- new output can still persist provider-materialized CardKit through the
  legacy Gateway View escape hatch;
- completion-choice submissions recursively embed prior Segment and Action Set
  identities. A live click produced a 296-character submission ID, Core
  returned `invalid_submission_identity`, the durable intent became
  `uncertain`, and the callback still returned a false success toast;
- completion wake-up ordering depends partly on a nullable
  `presentation_reply_id` rather than only on retention-safe prerequisite
  edges.

No additional Delivery Ledger or durable Ring snapshot is required. The
existing SQLite Outbox Entry can be deepened into the durable message/effect
record, while the Ring remains a disposable process-local MQ and the existing
scope checkpoint remains a derived recovery accelerator.

## Solution

Move the unification boundary to the committed Outbox Entry. New Turn Card
work persists a typed Delivery Subject and an immutable provider-neutral
Presentation Snapshot in the same transaction as the projection transition.
Only after commit may the complete work item enter the per-scope Ring.

The Ring consumer renders the frozen snapshot, prepares a Gateway effect, and
uses a second fenced compare-and-swap transaction to freeze the exact plan and
plan hash before any external call. Existing producers that have not migrated
presentation continue to enqueue already prepared effects through a
compatibility variant of the same Outbox Entry and use the same Ring,
execution, retry, settlement, and checkpoint machinery.

After Gateway execution, one SQLite-local settlement transaction records the
receipt and provider checkpoints, settles the exact typed subject and all
receipt-derived projection state, establishes successor prerequisites, and
recomputes the safe Delivery Ring Checkpoint. This transaction does not claim
cross-system exactly-once semantics: provider success followed by a crash
before local settlement remains an explicitly uncertain effect that cannot be
automatically replayed without provider-backed idempotency or positive
not-applied evidence.

Turn Card pagination moves behind a versioned Conversation Page Presentation
Policy. The policy plans in canonical source units, freezes a provider-neutral
snapshot, proves a conservative encoded-size bound, and later renders that
same snapshot into a Gateway View. Frozen pages are never replanned; existing
active pages remain on the legacy policy; only newly created pages enter the
new semantic-snapshot protocol.

The first vertical migration is Turn Card. Other producers retain their
current prepared-effect input until separately migrated, but they do not gain
another scheduler or durable authority. Completion-choice identity and
truthful callback feedback are repaired first because the live approval path
is currently unreliable.

## User Stories

### SCN-1: Reliable completion choice

When an authorized user selects a completion option after any number of prior
choice turns, Swarm creates one fixed-length deterministic Submission Intent,
submits it through Agent Input, and reports success only when the returned
durable state supports success. A definite pre-effect rejection reports
failure; an uncertain result reports that confirmation is pending and is not
automatically resubmitted.

### SCN-2: Commit before Ring admission

When projection work creates or updates a semantic Turn Card delivery, the
typed subject, frozen Presentation Snapshot, scope, order, idempotency
identity, and owner fence commit before the work enters a Ring. A rollback
produces neither durable work nor an external effect.

### SCN-3: Missed enqueue and Ring loss

If the process exits after SQLite commit but before Ring enqueue, or if Ring
capacity spills, startup/refill reconstructs complete work from SQLite after
the safe scope checkpoint. No second durable queue or Ring snapshot is needed.

### SCN-4: Consumer-time preparation

The consumer renders the frozen snapshot under its recorded renderer and
Gateway profile versions, verifies the committed presentation measurement,
and freezes the exact Gateway plan/hash in SQLite before the first provider
call. A crash before plan freeze safely rerenders the same snapshot; a crash
after plan freeze reuses the frozen plan.

### SCN-5: Concurrent newer revision

If a newer revision appears while an older Ring item exists, the preparation
CAS rejects stale work. An older effect may be superseded only when durable
evidence proves it not started. Prepared, claimed, uncertain, or delivered
effects are not mutated; a newer conflicting revision waits as a successor.

### SCN-6: Uncertain remote effect

If Feishu may have accepted an effect but SQLite lacks conclusive settlement,
the exact attempt becomes uncertain. Swarm preserves its attempt identity,
effect certainty, provider checkpoints, and owner fence and does not
automatically replay it unless the operation has a verified safe recovery
contract.

### SCN-7: SQLite-local atomic settlement

After a conclusive Gateway success, one local transaction records the Outbox
terminal state, provider receipt/checkpoints, durable target identities,
subject delivered revision, recovery/replacement completion, successor
prerequisites, and recomputed safe scope checkpoint. A process exit after this
commit but before an in-process wake does not require Page repair.

### SCN-8: Subject settlement gap

If a conclusive remote success cannot settle its exact subject because the
projection identity or revision is inconsistent, the external effect remains
delivered and is never replayed. Swarm records a durable settlement gap,
blocks later conflicting revisions of that subject, exposes the gap
operationally, and allows unrelated work to continue.

### SCN-9: Scope ordering and checkpoint recovery

Within one Delivery Scope, semantic-snapshot and legacy prepared entries share
the existing durable delivery order and one Ring. The Delivery Ring Checkpoint
represents only the derived contiguous terminal prefix. It never skips
uncertain, unresolved replacement, active quarantine, or reopened work and may
rebase backward.

### SCN-10: Stable canonical pagination

New pages use a versioned policy and canonical start/end anchors. Frozen pages
never change. Existing active legacy pages continue under the legacy policy
without fabricating missing modern plan metadata. Restart across renderer or
budget upgrades neither duplicates nor omits canonical content.

### SCN-11: Provider-neutral Turn Card

New semantic Turn Card durable state contains no raw CardKit, Lark SDK object,
opaque provider node, database row, mutable projection reference, or renderer
closure. The Feishu adapter alone materializes Gateway View into CardKit, and
the visible result remains equivalent to the current Turn Card.

### SCN-12: Retention-safe completion wake-up

The choice-bearing update depends on the exact page/card creation, and the
completion mention depends on the exact choice-bearing update reaching
`delivered`. These prerequisite edges survive restart, safe replacement, and
retention. The resulting wake-up remains ACK-gated and uses the concise text
`需要你的选择`.

### SCN-13: Forward-only mixed-version migration

Expansion adds nullable columns and readers without modifying immutable
historical prepared/claimed rows. New semantic pages enter through a durable
cohort marker only after shadow parity. Subjectless, compacted, uncertain, and
legacy rows remain executable or recoverable through their current contracts
and block contraction when still actionable.

### SCN-14: Observable safe cutover

Operators can see semantic/legacy counts, unsupported versions, oldest
unprepared work, CAS failures, uncertainty, settlement gaps, prerequisite lag,
retention blockers, checkpoint rebases, and shadow mismatches. Cutover and
contraction refuse to proceed while required safety conditions are not met.

## Implementation Decisions

### Domain Model

The affected bounded contexts remain Conversation Projection and Delivery and
Operations. Feishu is an outer Gateway adapter.

Conversation Projection owns Conversation Page and Page Plan. A Page Plan is a
versioned canonical-source interval under a typed Presentation Budget. The
Plan and its Presentation Snapshot describe desired visible state; they do not
prove any provider effect occurred.

Delivery and Operations owns the Outbox Entry as the delivery aggregate root.
For the new semantic variant it contains one immutable Delivery Subject and
Presentation Snapshot. During consumption it acquires one immutable Prepared
Delivery through a guarded `NULL -> frozen plan/hash` transition. The Entry
then owns claim, retry, effect-certainty, receipt, and terminal delivery state.

A Delivery Subject is a typed immutable value. The first supported subject is:

```ts
type ConversationPageSubject = Readonly<{
  kind: "conversation-page";
  segmentId: string;
  pageIndex: number;
  revision: number;
}>;
```

`projection_key` remains an idempotency/debug and legacy compatibility label;
new Turn Card execution does not parse it to recover subject identity.

A Presentation Snapshot is immutable provider-neutral semantic input. It
contains bounded timeline content, completion actions, trusted mention
identity, Goal, Task List, Session Activity/Subagents, continuation metadata,
and versioned presentation policy identity. It contains no provider payload.

The Delivery Ring is a bounded process-local MQ, full-data cache, and serial
external-effect executor for one Delivery Scope. Queue contents, local head
phase, credits, retry timers, byte accounting, and cooldown are disposable.

Gateway Effect Checkpoint and Delivery Ring Checkpoint are separate concepts:

- a Gateway Effect Checkpoint proves a sub-effect such as surface creation or
  stream application;
- a Delivery Ring Checkpoint is a derived, rebasable safe watermark for one
  scope's contiguous terminal prefix.

The following invariants are normative:

#### INV-1: Durable-before-Ring

A semantic Outbox Entry enters a Ring only after its projection and snapshot
transaction commits.

#### INV-2: Disposable Ring

Ring loss, overflow, missed wake, or restart can affect latency and reads but
cannot lose, mutate, or reorder durable work.

#### INV-3: Immutable snapshot

Subject, revision, snapshot schema/version, snapshot hash, planner version,
renderer version, Gateway profile, scope, order, idempotency key, and owner
fence describe one immutable desired effect.

#### INV-4: Durable plan freeze

The exact Gateway plan/hash commits through a CAS over the immutable snapshot
identity before any external call.

#### INV-5: No cross-system atomicity claim

Feishu success without local settlement remains uncertain and is not
automatically replayed without an approved safe recovery proof.

#### INV-6: Typed subject

New Turn Card claim and settlement use typed subject fields and never
reconstruct them from provider output or formatted keys.

#### INV-7: Safe revision replacement

An Entry is superseded only when its effect is durably proven not started;
otherwise a newer revision is a successor.

#### INV-8: Canonical pagination

Durable page boundaries use canonical source units and a versioned policy,
never transformed display length.

#### INV-9: Local atomic settlement

Every receipt-dependent SQLite fact and causally released successor commits
with the terminal Outbox transition.

#### INV-10: Derived checkpoint

A scope checkpoint is computed from the earliest authoritative nonterminal
row, may rebase backward, and is never advanced merely because a later order
ACKed.

#### INV-11: Retention barrier

Execution evidence, snapshots, plans, prerequisites, recovery lineage,
projection targets, and human-review state remain until their independent
correctness obligations are terminal.

#### INV-12: No Agent replay

Delivery retry, recovery, or choice feedback never resubmits an Agent Input
that may have reached Core.

#### INV-13: Retention-safe prerequisites

Dependent effects protect exact prerequisites through ACK, replacement,
restart, and retention.

#### INV-14: Bounded choice identity

Completion-choice submission and source identities are deterministic and
fixed-length; their size never grows with conversation depth.

### Architecture

The public flow is:

```text
Conversation Projection
  -> Delivery Intent Port
  -> SQLite Outbox Entry COMMIT
  -> post-commit Delivery Ring enqueue
  -> Unified Delivery Consumer
  -> Presentation Policy render/measure
  -> Gateway Delivery Port prepare
  -> SQLite CAS plan freeze
  -> Gateway Delivery Port execute
  -> SQLite-local settlement
  -> post-commit wake/refill
```

The Outbox Entry accepts a discriminated input:

```ts
type DeliveryInput =
  | Readonly<{
      kind: "semantic-snapshot";
      subject: DeliverySubject;
      snapshot: PresentationSnapshot;
      snapshotHash: string;
      plannerPolicyVersion: number;
      rendererPolicyVersion: number;
    }>
  | Readonly<{
      kind: "prepared-effect";
      effect: PreparedGatewayDelivery;
    }>;
```

New Turn Card uses `semantic-snapshot`. Unmigrated producers and historical
rows remain `prepared-effect`. Both converge to the same prepared claim,
execution, failure, checkpoint, and settlement machinery.

The Presentation Policy is one deep provider-neutral module:

```ts
interface ConversationPagePresentationPolicy {
  plan(input: PagePlanningInput): PlannedSnapshot;
  measure(snapshot: PresentationSnapshot): PresentationMeasure;
  render(snapshot: PresentationSnapshot): GatewayView;
}
```

`measure()` returns an encoded-size upper bound and element/action counts.
Planning and consumer verification use the same policy/version. The configured
Gateway profile reserves materialization overhead, and Feishu adapter contract
tests prove that actual CardKit serialization stays within the committed
bound. A mismatch is a deterministic not-started preparation failure and no
external call occurs.

The Delivery Store remains a deep module with a small consumer-facing
interface. Its implementation may be internally decomposed, but callers need
only reserve committed work, freeze a prepared effect, claim prepared work,
record provider checkpoints, settle an outcome, and page/reconcile scope
heads. SQL joins, legacy translation, prerequisite movement, recovery lineage,
and checkpoint derivation remain behind that seam.

Concrete dependency direction is:

```text
cards/presentation policy -> domain projection DTOs + Gateway View contract
delivery consumer         -> delivery ports + presentation policy + Gateway port
SQLite adapters           -> implement delivery/projection persistence ports
Feishu adapter            -> implement Gateway port and materialize Gateway View
composition               -> assemble concrete adapters and workflows
```

Coordinators and domain ports do not accept raw CardKit objects for the new
Turn Card path. Existing provider-shaped paths remain explicit compatibility
inputs and do not authorize new legacy payload production.

### Behavior & Failure Modes

The lifecycle is:

```text
reserved -> preparing -> prepared -> claimed
                                      |-> delivered
                                      |-> retry_wait (proven not-started)
                                      |-> uncertain
                                      |-> dead_letter
                                      `-> dismissed (proven not-started)
```

Reservation transaction A persists the semantic snapshot and projection
transition. Rendering occurs outside SQLite. Transaction B uses CAS over entry
state, subject/revision, snapshot hash, policy/profile versions, owner fence,
and current instance lease to freeze the plan/hash before execution. CAS
failure discards the stale Ring item.

Snapshot revision replacement follows these rules:

- reserved/preparing work may be atomically dismissed and replaced only when
  no external effect began;
- prepared work may be superseded only with durable `not-started` proof;
- claimed, uncertain, or delivered work is immutable, and a newer conflicting
  revision waits through a durable prerequisite;
- safe replacement atomically transfers conflict ownership and prerequisites
  and cannot leave the Ring head without durable terminal/replacement proof.

An expired claimed entry is retriable only when the specific operation has
provider-backed idempotency or positive not-applied evidence. Otherwise it
becomes uncertain. Ring serialization is not evidence that a remote effect did
not occur.

SQLite-local settlement includes Outbox terminal state, provider receipt and
Gateway Effect Checkpoints, message/card/surface/thread identities, subject
delivered revision, Page state, recovery/replacement completion, causally
released successor entries, and recomputed Delivery Ring Checkpoint. A
post-commit bus may wake work but owns no correctness transition.

If remote success cannot settle the exact subject, settlement marks the effect
delivered, records a typed projection/settlement gap, blocks later conflicting
subject revisions, and permits unrelated work. Repair uses durable receipt and
subject evidence, never the visible Feishu card as workflow truth.

Completion-choice handling first records the one-shot Action Set decision and
a bounded deterministic Submission Intent. Callback feedback uses the returned
Agent Input state: conclusive accepted states report success, `uncertain`
reports pending confirmation, and definite cancellation/rejection reports
failure. Existing uncertain intents are queried for receipts and are not
automatically resubmitted.

### Compatibility & Migration

Expansion adds nullable typed subject, semantic snapshot, snapshot hash,
policy/profile version, and preparation-state fields. Historical immutable
prepared/claimed rows are not backfilled or rewritten.

The migration matrix is:

| Existing row | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| pending prepared | execute through legacy prepared compatibility |
| claimed | preserve exact claim, plan, identity, and recovery semantics |
| uncertain | never auto-convert or replay |
| dead-letter with replacement | retain recovery lineage until discharged |
| delivered/dismissed | retain as legacy audit/retention data |
| compacted | never fabricate snapshot or typed subject |
| actionable without typed subject | continue legacy execution and block contraction |
| new semantic cohort row | require typed subject, snapshot, hashes, and versions |

The rollout is forward-only:

1. repair completion-choice identity and truthful callback feedback;
2. ship nullable schema and dual-shape readers with no semantic writers;
3. add Ring consumer preparation and plan-freeze support;
4. shadow-plan new Turn Card semantics and compare visible structure, target,
   scope/order, idempotency, and size bounds without executing the semantic
   entry;
5. enable semantic entries only for newly created cohort pages;
6. retain legacy active/frozen pages and all historical prepared rows;
7. contract legacy Turn Card dispatch only after zero actionable ambiguous
   rows, zero unsupported versions, zero unresolved semantic gaps, zero shadow
   mismatch, and successful backup/restore rehearsal.

Old binaries may operate only during the expansion phase while all new rows
remain legacy-readable. Once semantic rows are enabled, downgrade to an
unaware binary is unsupported; recovery requires a compatible release or the
approved database backup/restore boundary. Already committed semantic work is
never translated back to provider-shaped legacy payload.

Snapshot retention depends on lifecycle:

- before plan freeze, snapshot JSON, codec/version, policy version, and hash
  are execution-critical and cannot be compacted;
- after plan freeze, retry/restart use the frozen plan, but identity hashes and
  versions remain;
- preparation failures retain the snapshot until replacement, retry, or
  explicit dismissal becomes terminal;
- deletion requires terminal effect, terminal subject settlement, terminal
  dependents, discharged replacement/recovery lineage, terminal human-review
  obligations, and retention age.

Choice-bearing update and completion mention use formal durable prerequisite
edges. `presentation_reply_id` may remain a query convenience but is not the
sole correctness link. Safe replacement atomically transfers the edge;
retention protects the prerequisite until the dependent effect is terminal.

Operational cutover evidence includes semantic/legacy counts, subjectless and
snapshotless actionable rows, oldest unprepared age, versions in use, CAS
failures, uncertain effects, settlement gaps, unmet prerequisite age, shadow
mismatches, retention blockers, and checkpoint rebase counts.

## Testing Decisions

Behavior and persistence tests use the existing SQLite integration seams and
focused delivery/card tests before full verification.

- **SCN-1 / INV-12 / INV-14:** extend completion-choice store and card-action
  tests with many consecutive rounds; assert constant bounded identities,
  Core error classification, no automatic uncertain replay, and truthful
  toast results.
- **SCN-2 / INV-1 / INV-3:** verify projection plus semantic Outbox
  reservation commits atomically and rollback returns no post-commit work.
- **SCN-3 / INV-2:** reopen the database after commit-before-enqueue, exercise
  Ring overflow, and prove refill hydrates the exact immutable snapshot once.
- **SCN-4 / INV-4:** inject crashes before and after plan freeze; verify
  rerender only before freeze and exact plan/hash reuse afterward. Add stale
  snapshot/profile/renderer CAS rejection.
- **SCN-5 / INV-7:** test newer revisions during reserved, preparing,
  prepared, claimed, uncertain, and delivered phases, including atomic
  prerequisite/conflict transfer and no unsafe overwrite.
- **SCN-6 / INV-5:** inject provider success-before-local-ACK and expired
  claim cases; verify uncertain state, preserved checkpoints, and no replay.
- **SCN-7 / INV-9:** assert Outbox, provider identity, Page revision,
  recovery, successor prerequisite, and checkpoint changes are one SQLite
  transaction. Exit after commit and before wake; reopening must need no Page
  repair.
- **SCN-8:** force subject mismatch after conclusive provider success; assert
  delivered effect plus typed gap, blocked same-subject successor, and no
  external replay.
- **SCN-9 / INV-10:** test mixed semantic/legacy scope order, conflict-isolated
  bypass, old work reopening, backward checkpoint rebase, and earliest
  authoritative nonterminal selection.
- **SCN-10 / INV-8:** persist versioned canonical Page Plans; restart across
  renderer/budget changes; prove frozen and legacy active boundaries do not
  move and new pages use the new policy.
- **SCN-11:** add Gateway View equivalence and encoded-bound contract tests;
  reject raw CardKit/opaque nodes in new Turn Card durable rows.
- **SCN-12 / INV-13:** test exact creation -> choice update -> mention
  prerequisites across delayed ACK, restart, safe replacement, duplicate ACK,
  and retention cutoff.
- **SCN-13:** use old-schema and mixed-version database fixtures covering the
  complete migration matrix, immutable-row triggers, downgrade refusal, and
  forward-only recovery.
- **SCN-14:** test status/readiness/cutover refusal fields and bounded indexed
  scans. Add `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` assertions and production-shaped backlog
  timing for new subject/snapshot/prerequisite predicates.
- Add backup/restore rehearsal coverage for the contraction boundary.
- Keep architecture/import checks separate from behavior tests: new
  provider-neutral presentation modules cannot import Feishu/Lark adapter or
  SDK modules, and coordinators cannot accept raw CardKit on the semantic path.

Affected focused suites are expected to include
`tests/conversation-segment-store.test.ts`,
`tests/prepared-delivery-store.test.ts`, `tests/prepared-delivery-ring.test.ts`,
`tests/ring-delivery-hot-path.test.ts`, `tests/ring-delivery-recovery.test.ts`,
`tests/turn-card-workflow.test.ts`, `tests/turn-card.test.ts`,
`tests/gateway-view.test.ts`, card-interaction/choice tests, retention tests,
migration tests, operations/status tests, and architecture-boundary tests.

Before delivery, run focused affected suites, `npm run typecheck`,
`npm run build`, and the full `npm test` sequentially. Installation, live
smoke, deployment, and restart require separate authorization and operational
safety checks.




## Out of Scope

- Migrating Worker Card, Worker Task, Answer Stream, operations messages, or
  every producer to semantic snapshots in this change. They retain the
  prepared-effect compatibility input.
- Replacing SQLite, the per-scope Ring topology, the fenced instance lease, or
  the existing Gateway execution contract.
- Creating a Delivery Ledger, durable Ring queue snapshot, second scheduler,
  or another durable ordering authority.
- Reconstructing semantic snapshots from historical CardKit/provider payloads.
- Replaying or rewriting historical uncertain Agent Inputs or delivery
  effects.
- Claiming cross-system exactly-once delivery.
- Deploying, restarting the live service, pushing, opening a PR, deleting
  legacy data, or contracting compatibility code without separate authority.
